title: Cabin Air Filter: Removal and Installation
introduction:
The cabin air filter catches particles in the air used by the passenger-compartment ventilation system. Think of it as the screen door; the blower is the fan doing the moving. Keeping those jobs separate helps explain why changing a filter is not, by itself, a diagnosis of an airflow complaint.

I use the drawings to trace the access route beneath the right-hand passenger-side instrument panel: lower insulator, filter cover, then filter. Blue identifies the component being removed; magenta identifies the retainers to release. This guide covers removal and refitting, with the illustrations providing the component locations and withdrawal direction.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle so another person cannot start the engine during service; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury. For work underneath or around the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could start remotely at any time, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Protect eyes, hearing and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use the applicable protection may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Review the applicable safety references
items.detail: Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184) before beginning. The filter sequence accesses the cabin air path; refrigerant handling, heater-hose disconnection and electric booster-heater servicing are separate operations with their own precautions.

edits.text: Working beneath the right-hand (RH) passenger-side instrument panel, remove the retainers shown in the illustration, then remove the lower instrument panel insulator.
edits.why: The insulator is the first layer of access beneath the dashboard. I match its shape and highlighted retaining points to the drawing before removing it, so the surrounding dashboard trim stays out of the guessing game.

edits.text: Locate the cabin air filter cover shown beside the blower housing. Remove its highlighted retainer, then remove the cover.
edits.why: The long, ribbed cover closes the filter opening. Removing it exposes the filter without confusing the nearby blower housing or electrical components with the part being serviced.

edits.text: Withdraw the cabin air filter from its housing in the direction indicated by the arrows in the illustration.
edits.why: The exposed rectangular filter is the particle-catching element. The arrows show its route out of the opening; the neighboring housing remains in place.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: insert the cabin air filter into its housing, refit the filter cover and its retainer, then refit the RH lower instrument panel insulator and its retainers.
edits.why: Reassembly closes the filter opening before restoring the dashboard's lower insulator. Use the drawings to confirm that both covers and their retainers are back in their illustrated positions. This completes the removal-and-installation sequence; it does not establish whether an airflow complaint has been resolved.
